Organizing rule: each functionality is built up in TWO steps -- a MINIMAL prototype commit (smallest real slice) with its test, then a COMPLETION commit (the rest) with its test. Some commits are single (atomic removals, docs, one build tweak). Your spec entry has a "slice" field: minimal | completion | single.

SLICE SEMANTICS (critical -- this makes the series reviewable)
- slice=minimal: code genuinely does ONLY the small slice, and its test checks ONLY that slice. E.g. "Andes CSR drain+verify, min (mxstatus)" drains + verifies ONLY mxstatus (hand-coded, not the X-macro loop); "runtime crt0/UART, min" only makes vplat_hello print, no exit/file-io yet; "fixtures, min (one C fixture)" relinks ONE fixture. You author a genuinely reduced version, NOT the final file.
- slice=completion: expand the prior minimal slice to full final form and extend the test to cover all. After it, the touched file matches final MINUS still-later-feature parts.
- slice=single: author to final form minus later-feature parts, per construct. Removal commits ('refactor!: remove ...') delete the named subsystem.
- The construct field says exactly what reduced/full content to write and how to derive it from the final file.

INCLUDE/ SUBMODULE: at the ABI-pin commit (spec functionality abi-submodule, ~c010) replace the in-tree include/hybrid headers with the andesim_abi submodule using include_submodule_recipe: 'git rm -r' the in-tree headers, remove leftover include/, 'git -C /home/nick/work/andesim/include worktree add --detach /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim/include <v2 sha>', 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim add include' + the .gitmodules entry (copy from final tree). To advance the pin later (v3/v4/v5/v6 commits): 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim/include checkout <sha>' then 'git -C /tmp/claude-1002/-home-nick-work-andesim/669779f8-77ed-406b-ab12-a36a1624de65/scratchpad/wt/andesim add include'. Never make include/ a plain tracked dir after that.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. === final scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive the andesim hybrid Andes-CSR capability list from a core's config.inc.

The OFFLINE checker for the hybrid handoff. It mirrors, in Python, the C++ gate
logic the vsim engine compiles in (src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp +
andes_caps_config.hpp). At runtime the engine reports the same list via
`sim_<core> --describe` ("andes_csrs"), and the andesim driver uses it to skip
--verify on CSRs the engine lacks. Running this on the engine's own build
config.inc must produce the same list -- a drift guard between the offline
config and the built engine (the flywheel; see tests/andes_sim/
test_andes_sim_caps_parity.sh).

Each Andes CSR is gated by a config.inc feature: a core implements the CSR only
when its feature is configured in. Restoring/draining a CSR the core lacks can
hang the DM handshake, so the engine and this checker gate on the same map.

Self-contained: the config.inc parser below is ported from Andes'
cpu_config_to_march_converter (parse_inc / is_yes / _int), so this depends only
on the Python stdlib.

Usage:
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py <config.inc>                       # print the list
  config_inc_to_andes_caps.py --check <config.inc> <csr> [csr...]  # assert exact
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# --- config.inc parsing (ported from cpu_config_to_march_converter) ----------
_DEFINE_RE = re.compile(r'^\s*`define\s+(\w+)(?:\s+(.+?))?\s*(?://\s*(.*))?$')


def parse_inc(path) -> dict:
    """{macro: string-value} from a Verilog config.inc (`define KEY VALUE)."""
    out: dict = {}
    for line in Path(path).read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
        m = _DEFINE_RE.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1)
        raw = (m.group(2) or "").strip().rstrip(",")
        comment = (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        if not raw:                                   # bare `define NAME flag
            out.setdefault(name, "1")
            continue
        if raw.startswith('"') and raw.endswith('"'):  # quoted string
            out[name] = raw[1:-1]
            continue
        c = comment.strip().strip('"')                # numeric + // symbolic
        if c and " " not in c:
            out[name] = c
            try:
                int(raw, 0)
                out.setdefault(name + "_INT", raw)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            continue
        out[name] = raw                               # bare integer / token
    return out


def _str(cfg: dict, key: str) -> str:
    if key in cfg:
        return cfg[key].strip().strip('"')
    if key + "_INT" in cfg:
        return cfg[key + "_INT"].strip()
    return ""


def _int(cfg: dict, key: str):
    """Numeric view: prefer the _INT companion macro, else parse the value."""
    for k in (key + "_INT", key):
        if k in cfg:
            try:
                return int(cfg[k], 0)
            except ValueError:
                pass
    return None


def is_yes(cfg: dict, key: str) -> bool:
    s = _str(cfg, key).lower()
    if s in ("yes", "true", "on"):
        return True
    if s in ("no", "false", "off", ""):
        return False
    n = _int(cfg, key)
    return n is not None and n == 1


# --- Andes-CSR capability derivation -----------------------------------------
def _ecc_any(cfg: dict) -> bool:
    """mecc_code exists if ANY RAM block is configured with ECC (type != none)."""
    for blk in ("NDS_DCACHE_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_ICACHE_ECC_TYPE",
                "NDS_ILM_ECC_TYPE", "NDS_DLM_ECC_TYPE"):
        n = _int(cfg, blk)
        if n is not None and n > 0:
            return True
    return False


def _any_yes(cfg: dict, *keys: str) -> bool:
    return any(is_yes(cfg, k) for k in keys)


def gates(cfg: dict) -> dict:
    """Feature gates, mirroring andes_caps_from_config() in the vsim binary."""
    priv = _int(cfg, "NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS") or 1   # 1=M, 2=M+U, 3=M+S+U
    perf = is_yes(cfg, "NDS_PERFORMANCE_MONITOR")
    # Andes PMNDS scheme: the standard Sscofpmf extension REPLACES the Andes
    # counter CSRs (RTL existent_csr: PERFORMANCE_MONITOR & !SSCOFPMF).
    pmnds = perf and not is_yes(cfg, "NDS_SSCOFPMF_SUPPORT")
    return {
        "DSP":          is_yes(cfg, "NDS_DSP_SUPPORT"),
        "CODENSE":      is_yes(cfg, "NDS_CODENSE_SUPPORT"),
        "POWERBRAKE":   is_yes(cfg, "NDS_POWERBRAKE_SUPPORT"),
        "STACKSAFE":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_STACKSAFE_SUPPORT"),
        "PERF_MONITOR": perf,
        "PMNDS":        pmnds,
        "PMNDS_UMODE":  pmnds and priv >= 2,
        "PMNDS_SMODE":  pmnds and priv >= 3,
        "PMA":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PMA_ENTRIES") or 0) > 0,
        "ILM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_ILM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "DLM":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_DLM_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "ECC":          _ecc_any(cfg),
        # Zcmt (jvt): the RTL gates jvt on ZCE_SUPPORT (newer config.inc
        # generations carry the knob; older ones have none -- absent = off).
        "ZCMT":         is_yes(cfg, "NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT")
                        or is_yes(cfg, "NDS_ZCE_SUPPORT"),
        # umisc_ctl: spec ALT_FP_FMT | CST_CTL; RTL BFLOAT16_ARITH | ACE.
        "ALT_FP":       is_yes(cfg, "NDS_BFLOAT16_ARITH_SUPPORT")
                        or is_yes(cfg, "NDS_ACE_SUPPORT"),
        "ALWAYS":       True,
        # v4 M-ext gates.
        "UMODE":        priv >= 2,
        "SMODE":        priv >= 3,
        "TRIGGER":      (_int(cfg, "NDS_NUM_TRIGGER") or 0) > 0,
        "EPMP":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMEPMP", "NDS_EPMP"),
        "SMRNMI":       _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMRNMI", "NDS_RNMI"),
        "EXCSLVL":      (_int(cfg, "NDS_EXCSLVL") or 0) > 0,
        "CLIC":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_ECLIC", "NDS_CLIC"),
        "SMSTATEEN":    is_yes(cfg, "NDS_SMSTATEEN"),
        # CCTL: the RTL gates mcctl* on cache presence (no config generation
        # emits a dedicated NDS_CCTLCSR knob), so bind the cache sizes too.
        "CCTL":         _any_yes(cfg, "NDS_CCTLCSR", "NDS_CCTL")
                        or (_int(cfg, "NDS_ICACHE_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0
                        or (_int(cfg, "NDS_DCACHE_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "PPI":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_PPI_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0,
        "FIO":          (_int(cfg, "NDS_FIO_SIZE_KB") or 0) > 0
                        or is_yes(cfg, "NDS_FIO"),
    }


# (csr name, gate) in HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST order, then the PMA group markers --
# mirrors andes_caps.hpp andes_gate_for() + supported_andes_csr_names().
_CSR_GATES = [
    ("mxstatus",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("mpft_ctl",       "POWERBRAKE"),
    ("mclk_ctl",       "ALWAYS"),
    ("milmb",          "ILM"),
    ("mdlmb",          "DLM"),
    ("mecc_code",      "ECC"),
    ("mhsp_ctl",       "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_bound",      "STACKSAFE"),
    ("msp_base",       "STACKSAFE"),
    # The PMNDS counter block: SPA existence mmsc_cfg.PMNDS (& misa[20]/[18]
    # for the U/S members). jvt is Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT implied by
    # classic CoDense. All were over-claimed once and faulted the PB drain
    # sweep live (0x7D1 + jvt on premium, 0x7CF on advanced/Sscofpmf).
    ("mcountermask_m", "PMNDS_UMODE"),
    ("uitb",           "CODENSE"),
    ("jvt",            "ZCMT"),
    ("ucode",          "DSP"),
    ("pmacfg",         "PMA"),
    ("pmaaddr",        "PMA"),
    # v4 M-ext CSRs, in HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST order (gdb mnemonics, matching
    # supported_andes_csr_names which iterates that list after the Andes block).
    ("menvcfg",        "UMODE"),
    ("mseccfg",        "EPMP"),
    ("mcounteren",     "UMODE"),
    ("mcountinhibit",  "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter3",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter4",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter5",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmcounter6",   "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent3",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent4",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent5",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mhpmevent6",     "PERF_MONITOR"),
    ("mcounterwen",    "PMNDS_UMODE"),
    ("mcounterinten",  "PMNDS"),
    ("mcountermask_s", "PMNDS_SMODE"),
    ("mcountermask_u", "PMNDS_UMODE"),
    ("mnscratch",      "SMRNMI"),
    ("mnepc",          "SMRNMI"),
    ("mncause",        "SMRNMI"),
    ("mnstatus",       "SMRNMI"),
    # mnvec: spec "IM Requirement: Required", RTL unconditional -- base Andes
    # NMI state, NOT part of Smrnmi (registration-audit under-claim fix).
    ("mnvec",          "ALWAYS"),
    ("mrnxvec",        "SMRNMI"),
    ("mdcause",        "ALWAYS"),
    ("mslideleg",      "SMODE"),
    ("msavestatus",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msaveepc1",      "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavecause1",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msaveepc2",      "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavecause2",    "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavedcause1",   "EXCSLVL"),
    ("msavedcause2",   "EXCSLVL"),
    ("mtvt",           "CLIC"),
    ("mintthresh",     "CLIC"),
    ("mcirq_entry",    "CLIC"),
    ("mstateen0",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen1",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen2",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mstateen3",      "SMSTATEEN"),
    ("mcctlbeginaddr", "CCTL"),
    ("mcctldata",      "CCTL"),
    ("mppib",          "PPI"),
    ("mfiob",          "FIO"),
    ("tselect",        "TRIGGER"),
    ("tdata1",         "TRIGGER"),
    ("tdata2",         "TRIGGER"),
    ("tcontrol",       "TRIGGER"),
    ("mcontext",       "TRIGGER"),
    ("uzobctl",        "UMODE"),
    ("ucctlbeginaddr", "UMODE"),
    ("sleepvalue",     "UMODE"),
    ("umisc_ctl",      "ALT_FP"),  # existence: BF16|ACE, not U-mode
]


def supported_andes_csrs(cfg: dict) -> list:
    g = gates(cfg)
    return [name for name, gate in _CSR_GATES if g[gate]]


def main(argv: list) -> int:
    if argv and argv[0] == "--check":
        if len(argv) < 2:
            print(__doc__)
            return 2
        got = supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[1]))
        want = argv[2:]
        if got != want:
            print(f"MISMATCH\n  got:  {got}\n  want: {want}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print("OK: " + " ".join(got))
        return 0
    if len(argv) != 1:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    print(" ".join(supported_andes_csrs(parse_inc(argv[0]))))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

=== final tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_caps_parity.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Andes-CSR capability parity (the flywheel / drift guard).
#
# The offline deriver (scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py) computes, from a
# core's config.inc, which Andes CSRs it implements. The vsim
# engine compiles the SAME gate logic (src/hybrid/andes_caps*.hpp) and reports
# the list at runtime via `--describe` ("andes_csrs"). Fed the engine's OWN
# embedded build config.inc, the two must be byte-identical -- a disagreement
# means the resume/drain capability gate is wrong for that engine.
#
# Runs against EVERY built engine under $VSIM_BIN_DIR (each sim_* binary with
# a V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc beside it) -- a single hardcoded engine left
# new engines with zero parity coverage. Uses the engine's build config.inc
# (the exact blob the binary embeds), so offline and online share one source.
# The --describe half is opportunistic: it needs the engine rebuilt with the
# S3 describe change (a prebuilt binary that omits "andes_csrs" is skipped).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

DERIVE="$ROOT/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py"
[ -f "$DERIVE" ] || fail "missing deriver: $DERIVE"

VSIM_BIN_DIR="${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$ROOT/../vsim_andesim/build}"

checked=0
for ENG in "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_*; do
  [ -x "$ENG" ] || continue
  name=$(basename "$ENG")            # sim_<engine>
  engine=${name#sim_}
  # The engine's embedded config.inc (copied next to its Verilated objects).
  CFG="$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V$engine/obj_sc/config.inc"
  [ -f "$CFG" ] || fail "$name present but its build config.inc not found at $CFG"

  offline=$(python3 "$DERIVE" "$CFG") || fail "deriver failed on $CFG"
  [ -n "$offline" ] || fail "deriver produced an empty list for $CFG"

  online=$("$ENG" --describe 2>/dev/null \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(" ".join(json.load(sys.stdin).get("andes_csrs", [])))' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$online" ]; then
    echo "[skip] $name --describe has no andes_csrs (rebuild vsim with the S3 change)"
    continue
  fi

  [ "$online" = "$offline" ] || fail \
    "PARITY MISMATCH ($engine): --describe andes_csrs != offline deriver"$'\n'"  describe: $online"$'\n'"  offline:  $offline"
  echo "[ok] $engine: --describe == offline deriver"
  checked=$((checked + 1))
done

[ "$checked" -gt 0 ] || { echo "[skip] no built engines under $VSIM_BIN_DIR"; ok "andes caps parity (skipped)"; exit 0; }

.rw-r--r-- 1.5k 1002  8 Jul 13:20 tests/lib/log.sh
--- content ---
# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}
